headline: Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi-controlled Hodeidah in Yemen
summary: The Houthi government warns Riyadh will pay a 'heavy price' after airstrikes targeted telecommunications infrastructure and Kamaran Island.
details: Saudi Arabia has launched airstrikes on the Houthi-controlled city of Hodeidah in Yemen, according to the Iran-backed Houthi group.
The Houthi Foreign Ministry expressed outrage, warning that Riyadh will pay a 'heavy price' for the attacks carried out late Friday night.
Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV reported that telecommunications infrastructure and Kamaran Island were targeted, with at least one woman injured on the island.
Reuters reported explosions at the Hodeidah port, though the Saudi-led coalition has denied allegations of attacking the port itself.
Hodeidah is a critical port city for Houthi-controlled northern Yemen, serving as the primary entry point for commercial goods and humanitarian aid.
Major General Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, blamed the Houthis for the escalation, calling their attacks on ships in the Red Sea 'cowardly and reckless'.
Al-Maliki stated that the coalition will continue all necessary military measures and will respond without hesitation to any further hostile actions by the Houthi group.
caption:
Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi-controlled Hodeidah. The Houthis warn Riyadh will pay a 'heavy price'.

Saudi Arabia has launched airstrikes on the Houthi-controlled city of Hodeidah in Yemen, according to the Iran-backed Houthi group.

The Houthi Foreign Ministry expressed outrage, warning that Riyadh will pay a 'heavy price' for the attacks carried out late Friday night.

Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV reported that telecommunications infrastructure and Kamaran Island were targeted, with at least one woman injured on the island.

Reuters reported explosions at the Hodeidah port, though the Saudi-led coalition has denied allegations of attacking the port itself.

Hodeidah is a critical port city for Houthi-controlled northern Yemen, serving as the primary entry point for commercial goods and humanitarian aid.

Major General Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, blamed the Houthis for the escalation, calling their attacks on ships in the Red Sea 'cowardly and reckless'.

Al-Maliki stated that the coalition will continue all necessary military measures and will respond without hesitation to any further hostile actions by the Houthi group.

Source: Prothom Alo, Somoy News

headline_marked: 15 people stopped: [[BGB foils two push-in attempts]] by India's BSF
headline: 15 people stopped: BGB foils two push-in attempts by India's BSF
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh prevented 15 people from being pushed into the country through the borders in Chapainawabganj and Kushtia.
details: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) foiled two alleged attempts by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) to push 15 people into Bangladesh yesterday.
In Chapainawabganj, the BGB prevented seven men from entering the country near border pillar 219/24-R under the Charaldanga Border Outpost (BOP) around 6:30 am.
Lt Col Mohammad Ariful Islam Masum, commanding officer of BGB-16, stated that members of the BSF-12 Battalion's Tilashan Camp tried to push the seven men across the border.
In a separate incident in Kushtia’s Daulatpur upazila, the BGB foiled an attempt to push eight people into Bangladesh through a river around 5:10 am.
The BGB reported that members of the BSF’s Char Meghna Camp allegedly forced eight people—two men, four women, and two transgender persons—to swim across the river.
Faced with resistance from the BGB and local residents, the group was forced to swim back to the Indian side of the river.
caption:
15 people were stopped from being pushed into Bangladesh in two separate border incidents yesterday.

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) foiled two alleged attempts by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) to push 15 people into Bangladesh yesterday.

In Chapainawabganj, the BGB prevented seven men from entering the country near border pillar 219/24-R under the Charaldanga Border Outpost (BOP) around 6:30 am.

Lt Col Mohammad Ariful Islam Masum, commanding officer of BGB-16, stated that members of the BSF-12 Battalion's Tilashan Camp tried to push the seven men across the border.

In a separate incident in Kushtia’s Daulatpur upazila, the BGB foiled an attempt to push eight people into Bangladesh through a river around 5:10 am.

The BGB reported that members of the BSF’s Char Meghna Camp allegedly forced eight people—two men, four women, and two transgender persons—to swim across the river.

Faced with resistance from the BGB and local residents, the group was forced to swim back to the Indian side of the river.
